title: Task poll response
description: 200 response to POST /api/v1/tasks/poll. At most one task, and only a catalog type with schema-valid parameters: never a command, script, path, or executable name (FR-3.1). The same task is returned again while the agent holds it claimed and has not started it (for example after a restart), so the agent must check its ledger before running anything (P3-A02); a task the server knows has started is never returned. An expired task is never returned (AC-3.8).

task.description: The task to run, or null when there is nothing to do.

id.description: The task's id (a UUID). The agent records it in its ledger before running anything, never runs an id twice, and uses it in the start, progress, and result paths.

type.description: A catalog task type id. The agent refuses a type it does not implement or has not enabled locally (result outcome refused).

parameters.description: The task's parameters, valid against the type's closed schema in the server's catalog. The agent validates them again against its own embedded catalog and refuses them if they fail (invalid_params).

additionalProperties.description: A parameter value, valid against the catalog type's closed schema (docs/api/tasks/task-catalog.json): a string, integer, or boolean, never a list or an object.

timeout_seconds.description: The deadline: the task must finish within this many seconds of starting. Relative, so the agent's clock does not matter. The agent uses the lower of this and its catalog's timeout_seconds, terminates its own task when it runs over, and reports timed_out.

catalog_version.description: The catalog_version of the server's task catalog, which the parameters were validated against when the task was claimed.

poll_seconds.description: The poll interval the server wants, in whole seconds (Settings: Tasks, P3-S06; default 30). A hint: the agent clamps it to its own bounds, and an absent value leaves it at its configured interval. Additive (DEC-20).

cancel.description: Stop a running task (P3-S05): sent while the host's running task is of an interruptible type and an operator asked to cancel it, until the agent reports its result. The agent stops the task if it is still running and reports outcome cancelled; if the task has already ended, it reports the real outcome. Absent or null means no instruction. Never sent for a task whose type cannot be interrupted: that task runs to completion. Additive (DEC-20).

id.description: The id of the running task to stop.
